title: Delegated Access Reconciliation Playbook
content:
Purpose
This is a working playbook for running delegated access reconciliation across systems (IAM, Console, Dedicated control plane, internal admin tools) with an eye toward quarterly least-privilege recertification and privileged access audit readiness. The focus is on: 
- mapping RBAC v2 roles to entitlement sources,
- producing SIEM-friendly audit exports,
- automating evidence collection for quarterly recert runs, and
- triaging exceptions for delegated owners.

Context & motivation
We introduced RBAC v2 in 2025 with resource-scoped role bindings. That decouples permissions from org-level groups but increases the surface area for stale grants. Historically privileged recert tasks were manual and concentrated on central admin groups; with RBAC v2 we need distributed reconciliation and tooling to collect deterministic evidence for auditors. This doc ties the bits together and proposes a repeatable runbook.

High-level run cadence (recommended)
- Weekly: entitlement snapshot + top-100 anomalous grants (automated job). Owner: eng-sre.
- Monthly: delegated owners receive a digest and must acknowledge or revoke. Owner: delegated owners (product/team leads) with reminders from security.
- Quarterly: full recertification window (2 weeks), evidence bundle generation for auditors. Owner: security-and-compliance.

Runbook: automated snapshot -> triage -> recert window
1) Snapshot generation (automated)
   - Run 'ent-snap' job that queries: 
     * RBAC bindings API (rbac-v2) - produce role, subject, resource-id, grant-timestamp
     * Console-admins table (postgres) - list of admin_user_id, org_id, last_used_ts
     * Dedicated control plane ACLs (s3 export) - merge by principal id
   - Output format: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) with canonical fields: timestamp, principal_id, principal_type, role_id, resource_id, source_system, grant_id, grant_created_at, last_seen_activity
   - Persist snapshots for 90 days.

2) Enrichment & heuristics (automated)
   - Enrich principal_id -> user metadata from identity provider (email, hire_date, manager).
   - Add risk signals: last_activity_days, is_service_account, cross_region_grant, privilege_depth (how many high-risk roles attached).
   - Tag obviously stale grants: last_activity_days > 365 => stale_candidate.

3) SIEM export (for auditors and realtime detection)
   - Export nightly delta (new grants + revoked grants) to our SIEM via HTTPS ingest (JSON array). Use the following lightweight envelope: 
     {\"event_type\": \"entitlement.change\",\n       \"ts\": \"2026-02-20T02:00:00Z\",\n       \"principal_id\": \"u12345\",\n       \"subject_type\": \"user\",\n       \"action\": \"grant|revoke\",\n       \"role_id\": \"console/org-admin\",\n       \"resource_id\": \"org:acme-123\",\n       \"source\": \"rbac-v2-api\",\n       \"change_id\": \"chg-98765\",\n       \"metadata\": {\"last_activity_days\": 12, \"is_service_account\": false}\n     }

   - Note: SIEM requires flat fields for indexing. The ingest pipeline will flatten the top-level keys and index metadata.* into keyword/text depending on type. Avoid nested arrays in the envelope.

4) Evidence automation for quarterly recert
   - For each resource-owner pair flagged for recertification, we produce an evidence bundle: latest snapshot entries, activity logs (last 90 days), access request history (JIRA/Okta ticket), owner acknowledgment record (signed checkbox in console), and remediation ticket if found.
   - Evidence bundle filename convention: evidence_<resource>_<quarter>_<YYYYMMDD>.zip
   - Automation steps (implementation notes):
     * Lambda that composes the bundle from S3 paths (snapshots/, console-activity/, jira-attachments/).
     * Push bundle to internal evidence storage and add pointer to Confluence page for the quarter.

5) Delegated owner workflow (manual + automated)
   - Owners receive an email digest with: list of active principals on their resources, suggested removals (stale + low usage + high-risk), and one-click actions: confirm/no-action/request-more-info.
   - If owner does nothing for 7 days, generate a security task for their manager and secondary owner.

Sample queries & detection heuristics
- SIEM correlation rule (pseudo-SPL) to detect rapid-grant bursts:
  index=entitlements (source:entitlement.change) | stats count by principal_id, role_id, _time span=1h | where count > 5

- Postgres query (console-admins) to find admin-like accounts with no activity in 180 days:
  SELECT user_id, email, last_used_ts FROM console_admins WHERE last_used_ts < NOW() - INTERVAL '180 days';

- RBAC API example (ndjson) entry (canonical):
  {\n    \"timestamp\": \"2026-02-19T23:55:12Z\",\n    \"principal_id\": \"svc-deploy-001\",\n    \"principal_type\": \"service_account\",\n    \"role_id\": \"deploy/runner\",\n    \"resource_id\": \"proj:infra-x\",\n    \"source_system\": \"rbac-v2\",\n    \"grant_id\": \"g-20260219-0001\",\n    \"grant_created_at\": \"2024-08-11T14:22:00Z\",\n    \"last_seen_activity\": \"2026-01-15T12:11:00Z\"\n  }

Triage and exception handling (playbook rules)
- Fast path: auto-revoke if service_account AND last_seen_activity > 365 days AND no linked rotate policy.
- Owner-reviewed path: flagged items go to owner's digest. If owner explicitly verifies within recert window -> mark evidence=\"owner_verified\".
- Compliance escalation: if an owner is unresponsive and grant is high-risk (role in high_privilege_list), create SEC ticket and begin forced deprovision after 14 days.

Audit log schema (recommended minimal set)
- event_id (string)
- event_ts (ISO8601)
- actor_id (string) -- who performed the action (can be system)
- actor_type (string) -- user|service|system
- action (string) -- grant|revoke|modify
- target_principal (string) -- principal receiving the entitlement
- target_type (string) -- user|service|group
- role_id (string)
- resource_id (string)
- source_system (string)
- change_id (string)
- reason (string, optional)
- request_ticket (string, optional) -- jira/okta ID
- raw_payload (string, optional) -- stringified JSON of original API payload

Notes on retention & privacy
- Retain entitlement change logs for 3 years to support audits. Snapshots are kept 90 days (for operational rollback). Evidence bundles saved per-quarter for 7 years (audit requirement).
- Mask PII in SIEM exports (email addresses) by hashing prior to transmit; keep mapping in internal secure store.

Open questions / To resolve
- How do we canonicalize service-account identities across systems (console vs dedicated vs infra)? Current mapping heuristics are fragile. Owner: Ethan Zhao.
- Confirm legal retention windows for evidence bundles vs logs (security-and-compliance to confirm with legal). Owner: Maya Rivera.
- SLA for owner response during quarterly recert (suggest 10 business days) - need leadership sign-off. Owner: Asha Patel.

Action items (next sprint)
- [ ] Implement ent-snap job with ndjson output and 90d retention (eng-infra).
- [ ] SIEM ingest adapter: validate flattening pipeline & field mappings (eng-security).
- [ ] Owner digest email templates + one-click API endpoints (console-and-tooling).
- [ ] Auto-bundle composer lambda and Confluence pointering (product-security).

Appendix: quick cheat sheet for delegated owners (to be used in digest)
- \"Verify\" = I confirm these principals need access.
- \"Revoke\" = Remove access immediately (preferred for stale/service accounts).
- \"Ask for more info\" = Send back to security for deeper analysis.

Example owner digest excerpt:
- resource: proj:payments-backend
  * alice@redwood.ai (user) - role: proj/developer - last_activity: 3d - action: no_action
  * svc-kafka-producer (service_account) - role: proj/io-producer - last_activity: 430d - action: suggested_revoke (auto-revoke criteria met)

Historical notes
- Borrowed some heuristics from the 2024 least-privilege run (manual) but this playbook is the first attempt to systematize delegated reconciliation across RBAC v2.

If you are reading this and own a product area: please review the sample digest and volunteer for a pilot recert window (Q2-2026).

-- Asha (security)
Notes: draft; rough TODOs inline; will move to a formal runbook after the pilot completes.
